conflicts.summary: 2026-10-06 brief treated treemap/sunburst as optional examples; 2026-10-10 feedback makes them the goal.
conflicts.resolution: Later explicit feedback wins; first shape (pivot subtotals) discarded.

shape.appetite: Medium: one new chart type with three layouts over a shared hierarchy model; 2–3 levels × 2–8 categories.
shape.problem: There is no way to see nested category sizes and part-to-whole relationships as a chart.
shape.recommended_shape: One Hierarchy chart type with an arrangement setting (treemap, then icicle, then sunburst) and zoom with breadcrumbs, over a shared builder for path identity, sizes, Other, missing values, focus, filters, and tracing. Focus is stored as focus?: datum[] values along levels.

counterproposal.statement: Register separate Treemap, Sunburst, and Icicle chart types.
counterproposal.rejected_because: Changing chart type resets settings except field, so users lose levels on every switch; all the hard logic is shared anyway. Separate Add Chart entries can still preset the layout.

superseded_shape.summary: Pivot Table subtotals, collapse, and share of parent.
superseded_shape.reason: User wants hierarchical charts, not Excel-style pivot complexity.

success_moves: One chart type with a layout setting — reduces: Losing setup when switching layouts; three copies of selection and trace logic; benefit: Each later layout is mostly geometry

Pure hierarchy builder (rows → path nodes with value, share of parent, share of whole, Other, missing) tested without the browser — reduces: Wrong totals or merged repeated labels hidden behind visuals; benefit: Fast vitest loop; pivot of same fields is the oracle
Reuse Sankey category-path conventions and its field-value filter model — reduces: Inconsistent missing/Other behavior across path charts; benefit: Familiar settings; no new filter type

Limit multi-select to whole branches and same-parent siblings — reduces: Cross-combination selections from independent field filters; benefit: Exact selection without waiting on precise-composite-selection
Ship treemap first; add sunburst and icicle only after the proof — reduces: Three renderers built before labels and small-node handling are proven; benefit: Valid intermediate state after one layout

Store focus as a raw value path along levels, resolved before Other grouping — reduces: nondeterministic or layout-dependent zoom state; benefit: same view after reload, readable in dashboard text, survives filters

first_proof.question: Does the shared hierarchy model produce correct totals and exact branch selection?
first_proof.artifact: Two-level treemap on shop-10000 (Region → Category, sum of Revenue) with readouts and click-to-filter
first_proof.observation: Branch % of whole matches a pivot of the same fields; North › Home filters a rows table to exactly those orders
first_proof.decision_rule: Both hold → proceed to three levels/small categories, then icicle, then sunburst. Either fails → fix the shared model before adding layouts.

rabbit_holes: Label fitting and truncation in small or curved marks
Color assignment stability across filters and layouts
Double-click colliding with the first click selection and undo history

resolved_decisions.decision: No circle packing; rectangular first; sunburst last and cuttable
Zoom with breadcrumbs ships in the first wave; focus stored as a value path
Three-level hierarchies default to treemap; zoom covers narrow cards

zoom_rules: View only; does not filter other charts
Double-click a parent or Shift+Enter; Other and leaves are not zoomable
Unresolvable focus shows the deepest ancestor with rows and keeps the stored path
Changing levels keeps only the unchanged prefix
